\documentclass{article}
\title{Community Health-Worker Support in Two Provinces: A Three-Year Proposal}
\author{M. Abera and J. Okafor}
\date{May 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Background}
The two target provinces have fewer than one community health-worker
per two thousand residents, and attrition among trained workers exceeds
twenty percent per year. Clinic catchment areas are large, referral
chains are long, and routine reporting reaches the district bureau with
months of delay. Any intervention that does not first stabilise the
workforce will be built on sand.

\section{Objectives}
The cornerstone of this proposal is the community health-worker
training programme: every other activity depends on trained workers
being present in the clinics, it consumes the largest share of the
budget, and its failure would make the remaining activities pointless.
The second pillar, which only makes sense once training is underway, is
the routine data collection pipeline, because the pipeline's value
stands or falls with the workers who feed it. The third and least
resource-intensive activity is the series of dissemination workshops,
which package whatever the first two have produced for district health
bureaus.

\section{Work packages}
\begin{itemize}
\item Dissemination workshops for district health bureaus in both provinces.
\item Routine data collection pipeline with monthly reporting.
\item Community health-worker training programme covering 240 workers.
\end{itemize}

\section{Budget sketch}
Roughly two thirds of the budget goes to training stipends, trainers
and training materials. The data pipeline accounts for most of the
remainder, covering devices, connectivity and a part-time data clerk
per district. The workshops are a rounding error by comparison, funded
from the dissemination line.

\section{Risks}
The main risk is attrition during the training year, which we mitigate
with staggered cohorts. A secondary risk is device failure in the data
pipeline, mitigated by keeping a paper fallback for the first six
months. No material risk attaches to the workshops, which can be
rescheduled at negligible cost.

\section{Timeline}
Year one is dominated by recruitment and the first two training
cohorts. The data pipeline pilots at the end of year one and scales
during year two. Dissemination workshops are scheduled for year three,
once there is something to disseminate.

\end{document}
